sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or give reasons).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Poor agricultural practices lead to soil ________ and decrease soil ________. (b) Floods, famine and strong winds are called ________ disasters.
Match Column A with Column B. A: (a) Polythene bags (b) Traditional chullah. B: (i) Smokeless chullah (ii) Paper bags (iii) Leaded petrol.
True or False. (a) Chemical fertilisers kill soil micro-organisms. (b) The Eco Mark certifies minimum pollution standards in production, packaging and disposal.
Rearrange the letters. (i) Avoid cutting trees: NTOSIFEAORTED (ii) Eco-friendly cooking fuel: SGAOIB (iii) Recycling household waste: EAMUNR.
questions.answer: (i) Afforestation (or deforestation to be avoided). (ii) Biogas. (iii) Manure.

questions.q: Name the practices that cause air degradation and the one that causes land degradation. Choose from smoking, spitting, loud music, open defecation.
questions.answer: Air degradation: smoking and loud music. Land degradation: spitting and open defecation.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: How does technical advancement contribute to environmental degradation?
questions.answer: Industries, mines and vehicles release toxic wastes, harmful gases and radioactive pollutants. These deplete the ozone layer and kill life in air, water and land.

questions.q: Ramesh wants to dispose of dry leaves and kitchen waste from his garden in an eco-friendly way. Which practice should he adopt and what is one benefit?
questions.answer: He should make compost in a compost pit. The compost is a manure that increases soil fertility and saves on chemical fertilisers.

questions.q: What do you understand by 'environmental degradation'? Mention its three natural causes.
questions.answer: It is an unfavourable change of our surroundings. Natural causes are earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and floods (also famine and strong winds).

questions.q: Why are forests called 'oxygen banks'?
questions.answer: Forests supply oxygen, influence rainfall and temperature, and prevent soil erosion. They also recharge water sources and shelter wildlife.

questions.q: Name any two effects of the depletion of the ozone layer.
questions.answer: More ultraviolet rays reach the earth, causing skin cancer and eye problems like cataract. They also stunt the growth of plants.

questions.q: What is 'eco friendly'? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Products and practices not harmful to the environment in production, use and disposal. Paper bags and unleaded petrol are examples.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the causes of environmental degradation (any three).
questions.answer: (i) Uncontrolled population growth increases demand for food, fuel and space and leads to deforestation and slums. (ii) Technical advancement releases toxic wastes and harmful gases. (iii) Poor agricultural practices and improper personal habits degrade soil, water and air.

questions.q: Explain the effects of deforestation (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Landslides, floods and soil erosion. (ii) No rainfall and drying of springs, lakes and rivers, changing the climate. (iii) Extinction of wildlife and reduced availability of land.

questions.q: How can an individual help in environmental conservation? (three points)
questions.answer: (i) Follow the 3 R's of reduce, reuse and recycle and use solar cookers. (ii) Use public transport or share cars and plant a tree. (iii) Keep the family small, save water and avoid smoking and loud speakers.

questions.q: Explain the role of the government in controlling environmental degradation (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Enforce strict pollution control laws and ensure waste treatment plants in industries. (ii) Provide efficient waste disposal and promote biogas and solar devices. (iii) Educate people, promote healthy farm practices and tree planting, and conserve wildlife.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the effects of air and water degradation on human life.
questions.answer: (i) Air: acid rain damages plants, animals and monuments like the Taj Mahal. (ii) The ozone layer is depleted, causing skin cancer and eye problems. (iii) Global warming raises temperature and makes rainfall unpredictable. (iv) Man-made disasters such as Bhopal and Chernobyl kill and harm life. (v) Water: sewage causes jaundice, diarrhoea, typhoid and malaria. (vi) Industrial wastes cause cancer, leukaemia and allergies and foam cuts oxygen for aquatic life.
